item.title: US lawmakers summon Nvidia ex-CEO after affair with suspected spy
item.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. “Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote Thursday on X. Scott said he was requesting Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. Nvidia hit gold when the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022 sparked a global rush to develop AI, with its processors — once designed for video game graphics — becoming a crucial ingredient to train and run the technology. – Informal Trump adviser – Nvidia did not give a reason for the departure of Huang, who also gave up his board seat. Huang is Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”. But he said the board had done what it needed: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: [2027] NASS condemns electoral violence nationwide
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the National Assembly condemning nationwide violence linked to the 2027 general elections. Another headline features President Bola Tinubu begging voters in Edo State during a campaign rally to re-elect him so he could complete ongoing projects. Vanguard also reports that ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has begun deploying non-sensitive materials nationwide. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian reports that violence threatens credible polls in 2027 as the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) trade blame over an attack during a town hall meeting organised for NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Lagos. The Punch leads with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) fixing November 28, 2026, for a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections to test upgrades to its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and electronic results transmission. Lastly, Daily Trust reports that bread makers have lamented the high cost of borrowing and rising operating expenses, warning that the combination of expensive credit, energy costs and increasing prices of production inputs is threatening the survival of bakeries across the country. item.title: Abductors of FUNAAB graduate, three others demand N500m ransom
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The abductors of a recent graduate of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), Adedoja Hannah, and three other individuals have reportedly demanded a ransom of N500 million for their release. The victims were allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday night when suspected gunmen invaded a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta, Ogun State, where they were working. The development was disclosed by the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of FUNAAB in a statement posted on its official Facebook platform on Thursday, expressing concern over the safety of the victims and appealing to members of the university community and the general public to remain calm. According to the union, Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, was among the four people abducted during the incident. Providing an account of the circumstances surrounding her disappearance, the union stated that Hannah was last seen on Monday, while her telephone has remained unreachable since the reported abduction. The statement partly reads, “The Students’ Union Government wishes to update the FUNAAB community and the general public on the abduction of Adedoja Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), alongside three other individuals at a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta. “According to information received, the incident occurred on Tuesday night when suspected kidnappers reportedly invaded the farm where the victims were working. Hannah was last seen on Monday, and her phone has remained unreachable since the incident. “Further information indicates that the abductors have demanded a ransom of ₦500 million for the release of all four victims. This development has understandably heightened concerns over their safety and the circumstances surrounding the incident. “The incident was reported to the appropriate security authorities, and the police have been working on the matter since Tuesday. Security efforts are ongoing, with attention directed towards locating the victims and securing their safe release. “We understand the concern this incident has generated, particularly among residents and members of the university community around the Alabata axis. However, we appeal to everyone to remain calm and allow the relevant authorities to carry out their investigations and response. “It is equally important that information shared publicly is accurate and responsible. Unverified reports and speculation should be avoided, especially where they could interfere with ongoing security efforts. “The Union is deeply concerned about the safety of Hannah and the other victims. item.title: ‘Years of injustice’ fuel northern Nigeria violence, says bandit leader
item.description: Decades of discrimination and extortion against Fulani herders are stoking the growing violence in northern Nigeria — unrest which will only swell until authorities tame the rampant corruption in the region, a bandit kingpin told AFP in a rare interview. Northwest and central Nigeria have for years been terrorised by gangs known locally as “bandits”, who raid villages, rustle cattle, conduct kidnappings and impose “taxes” on farmers and miners. The interview with one such gang leader came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, in a piece published Thursday, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and AFP northern Nigeria reporter Aminu Abubakar. “Years of injustices are what pushed Fulani herders into banditry. We were never criminals before,” a bandit leader named Babangida said. Banditry traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders. The conflict has spiralled from raids and revenge attacks into broader, complex criminality by gangs numbering from around a dozen to well into the hundreds. They have created a kidnapping economy that raises hundreds of thousands of dollars, and at times entered alliances with Nigerian jihadists. After months of negotiation, Babangida agreed to an interview in a remote Katsina state village, following the intervention of a former government peace negotiator. “Justice is the only way out. When justice is upheld, everyone will live in peace,” said the bandit, who asked only to be identified by his first name. In the meantime, violence reigns: last week, in neighbouring Zamfara state, bandits set fire to a home during a raid, killing a family of 12. Earlier this month, gunmen killed eight police officers, and in September, more than 80 people, mostly women, were kidnapped in Zamfara and Niger states — many while working their fields. Worsening insecurity has become a major issue in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. – Corruption – Clad in a blue kaftan, the 38-year-old passes for a normal villager, save for the Kalashnikov rifle in his hand. “No bandit just picked up a gun overnight and turned to violence. There is always a story behind it,” said Babangida, sheltering from the scorching heat under a neem tree. Babangida said he turned to banditry a decade ago after his family’s 97 cows were seized by a team of police and vigilantes. He described the raid as based on indiscriminate suspicions that all Fulani are bandits. He was forced to pay millions of naira (thousands of dollars) to post bail for his mother and brother. He only recovered 10 cattle, which he used “to buy guns, one of which I’m holding now” and moved his family to a camp in the bush. item.title: INEC warns Okada riders against political violence in Oyo
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators in Oyo State against allowing politicians to use them as instruments of violence, thuggery and electoral malpractice ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission urged members of transport unions to resist attempts to involve them in activities capable of undermining public peace and the credibility of the electoral process before, during and after the elections. The Oyo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Adeniran Tella, gave the warning on Thursday at the 2026 Day celebration of the Amalgamated Commercial Tricycle and Motorcycle Owners, Repairs and Riders Association of Nigeria (ACOMORAN), held alongside the launch of a book authored by the union’s chairman, Solomon Olugbode, at the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium, Oke-Ado, Ibadan. Tella, who was represented by the Head of INEC’s Information Unit, Olayiwola Awolowo, also urged members of the association to encourage their passengers and other members of the public to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). He stressed the importance of civic participation in the electoral process, saying commercial transport operators had a responsibility to protect democracy rather than allow themselves to be recruited into activities capable of threatening national security. “Let me be clear, do not allow yourselves to be used as instruments of violence or thuggery. The Nigeria Police Force has warned that the law will take its full course against anyone, no matter their status, who threatens public peace or engages in criminal conduct before, during or after the elections,” he said. Specifically, he charged ACOMORAN members to shun political violence, warning them against transporting weapons, money for vote-buying or individuals intending to disrupt the elections. “Your motorcycle or tricycle is a tool of livelihood, not a weapon of destruction. I urge you to remain politically neutral as a union,” he added. The INEC representative also cautioned the association against allowing its structures and operational resources to be deployed in support of any political party, noting that members retained the right to support candidates of their choice in their individual capacities. “While you have the right to support any candidate of your choice as individuals, the union’s infrastructure must never be hijacked to favour one party over another,” he said. He urged the transport operators to support INEC’s election logistics by ensuring the timely and safe movement of electoral materials and personnel whenever engaged by the commission. He also called on members to serve as voter education ambassadors by promoting peace, tolerance and responsible voting at motor parks and among their passengers. item.title: Protesters block INEC chair’s vehicle in London, demand resignation
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, was confronted by protesters in London on Thursday over alleged irregularities in the preliminary voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The demonstrators surrounded the vehicle conveying Amupitan outside Chatham House, where he was expected to participate in a panel discussion on Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 polls. The protesters, believed to be Nigerians living abroad, shouted insults at the INEC chairman and accused the commission of abandoning its neutrality in favour of President Bola Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress. They also demanded Amupitan’s resignation, labelling INEC a “criminal organisation” over alleged duplicate voter registrations, questionable polling units and photographs suspected to have been generated using artificial intelligence. The demonstration followed mounting criticism of the commission after images and records purportedly showing suspicious entries in the preliminary voters’ register circulated publicly. INEC had acknowledged irregularities in the registration process and announced an investigation into the affected records, further fuelling the controversy. ‘Trust me I won’t fail you’ Speaking earlier at the event, Amupitan asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude, whereas results in Anambra and Osun were declared the day after voting under his watch. item.title: Anambra requires 1,000 megawatts of electricity to power its growing economy – Soludo
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo has said that the state requires about 1,000 megawatts of electricity to adequately power its growing economy. Delivering the keynote address at the Electricity Market Investment Roundtable organised by the Anambra State Electricity Regulatory Commission (ASERC) in Awka, the governor lamented that Anambra currently receives only about 120 megawatts, describing the huge gap as both a major challenge and an investment opportunity. “Without electricity, there will be no manufacturing. Without energy, only little can happen. For us, it is very consequential. We are here to do business. Anambra is ready for business,” the governor declared. Soludo urged investors to take advantage of the numerous opportunities in the state’s electricity market, particularly those connected with the state’s proposed Mixed Industrial City and aerotropolis. The governor threw open the state’s electricity market to investors, declaring that Anambra is ready for business as it seeks to bridge a massive power deficit threatening its industrial and economic growth. To the participants at the summit, Soludo added: “Tell us when, where and how we can get the 1,000 megawatts. Let’s get the plan, a clear roadmap, actionable, verifiable roadmap. Anambra is a land of opportunities. This is a summit for closing deals. Let’s get it done. “Move beyond discussions and produce a practical, measurable and verifiable roadmap for closing the state’s electricity gap.” The governor reiterated his administration’s determination to create an enabling environment for private-sector participation in the electricity market. Chairman of Anambra State Electricity Regulatory Commission, ASERC, Professor Frank Okafor, commended the governor for driving innovation and reforms in the state’s energy sector. He acknowledged the substantial electricity deficit in Anambra, explaining that the roundtable was convened to bring stakeholders together to develop practical solutions to the challenge. “We are here to think together and come up with a solution that will help to overcome the challenge,” Okafor said. Former chairman of the Nigeria Communications Commission, NCC, Engr. Ernest Ndukwe, who chaired the event, noted that Governor Soludo has the capacity to deliver the changes required in the state’s electricity sector. He expressed personal interest in participating in the emerging electricity market, adding, “I want to be a player in the electricity revolution that is coming up in Anambra State.” He advised the state government to consider taking equity stakes in companies investing in electricity infrastructure in Anambra State, describing such participation as a strong vote of confidence that could encourage other investors. item.title: Swiss woman evacuated from Nigeria over Ebola discharged in Geneva
item.description: A Swiss woman who contracted the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola linked to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has been discharged from hospital in Geneva, Switzerland. The woman, who is the wife of a Swiss embassy employee in Abuja, was evacuated from Nigeria alongside her husband on October 26 after contracting the virus. Benoit Carpentier, spokesperson for the University Hospitals of Geneva (HUG), said the patient received supportive medical care, including hydration and management of potential complications associated with the disease. “The patient has recovered. She was discharged from hospital yesterday (Wednesday),” he told AFP, confirming a report by Tribune de Genève. The woman’s husband reportedly showed no symptoms of the disease, while his quarantine was lifted on November 4. Nigeria announced the Ebola case on October 20, confirming that it involved the Bundibugyo strain, the same variant responsible for the latest outbreak in the DRC. The strain remains a major public health concern as there is currently no specific approved treatment or vaccine against it. The outbreak was officially detected in the DRC in May and has since infected more than 11,000 people, with over 5,400 deaths recorded. Cases have also been detected in Uganda and Kenya, raising concerns about the spread of the disease across the region. item.title: Nigeria taking religious violence more seriously after US CPC listing – Officials
item.description: US State Department officials have said Nigeria is taking religious violence more seriously following its designation as a Country of Particular Concern (CPC) by President Donald Trump, but warned that more concrete action is needed to protect vulnerable communities and bring perpetrators to justice. The officials made the assessment on Thursday during a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s response to attacks on vulnerable communities since the US placed the country on its CPC list. President Trump redesignated Nigeria as a CPC over allegations of Christian persecution and genocide before the US military launched a missile strike against terrorist targets in Sokoto State on Christmas Day. Nigeria and the US have since entered into a military partnership targeting terrorists in the country’s northern region and established a joint working group to address Washington’s concerns over religious violence. The hearing was convened by Chris Smith, Chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Africa Subcommittee, to examine Nigeria’s response to attacks on vulnerable communities following the CPC designation. Speaking at the hearing, Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, said the State Department had intensified engagements with Nigerian officials to address attacks against Christian communities and ensure accountability for perpetrators. He, however, acknowledged that the violence had persisted, stressing that Washington expected measurable improvements in security deployments, early responses to warnings of impending attacks and prosecution of those responsible. “We are expecting results — protection for Christian communities in the Middle Belt through increased Nigerian security and law enforcement deployments, more timely and effective responses to early warnings of impending attacks, accountability for perpetrators through stronger courts and security services, and deeper military-to-military cooperation,” he said. Garcia said the US was pursuing a coordinated approach to strengthening Nigeria’s security architecture through capacity building, expanded use of biometric data to identify perpetrators and financial action plans to disrupt terrorist financing networks. “Though Nigeria has reported progress, under Secretary Hooker made it clear in the joint working group second session that this pace is insufficient,” he added. Also speaking, Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour, said the US had continued to urge the Nigerian government to repeal blasphemy laws or, at the minimum, stop enforcing them. Barnes said Trump’s redesignation of Nigeria as a CPC had prompted the country to take religious violence and related concerns more seriously. “The government has reported leadership changes, strategically deployed military forces, and increased arrests and prosecutions,” he said. item.title: Fasoranti’s death ends an era, says Akure communities
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Akure Speaking Communities Development Initiative (ASCDI) has described the death of Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, as the end of an era of wisdom, exemplary leadership, patriotism and selfless service to Akureland, Yorubaland and Nigeria. The group said the late elder statesman was a moral compass whose life and leadership inspired generations, describing his death as a profound loss to the people of Akure, the Yoruba nation and the country. In a condolence statement issued in Akure and signed by its Chairman, Air Commodore Adewale Ogunmodede (retd.), and Secretary, Dr Olawale Ademola, ASCDI said it received the news of his passing with profound sorrow. It described Fasoranti as an illustrious son of Akureland, a respected statesman and a distinguished Yoruba leader. “Pa Fasoranti was not merely an elder statesman; he was a moral compass, a symbol of courage, an embodiment of integrity, and a custodian of the cherished values and traditions of our people. “His life represented the finest ideals of community service, peaceful coexistence, justice, unity, and the pursuit of collective progress,” the statement said. The organisation noted that as leader of Afenifere and a prominent voice in national affairs, Fasoranti devoted much of his life to championing the interests of the Yoruba people, promoting democratic ideals and advocating fairness, equity and good governance in Nigeria. For the Akure Speaking Communities across Ifedore, Akure North and Akure South Local Government Areas of Ondo State, ASCDI said his death represented an immeasurable loss. It described him as a towering figure whose wisdom, experience and fatherly guidance inspired generations of leaders and community development advocates. “His enduring legacy reminds us that true greatness is measured not by personal accomplishments alone, but by the positive impact one makes on society and the values one leaves behind for succeeding generations,” it added. The group urged sons and daughters of Akure Speaking Communities, both at home and in the diaspora, to honour his memory by strengthening their commitment to unity, peaceful coexistence, cultural preservation and sustainable community development. It also extended its condolences to the Fasoranti family, the Deji and other royal fathers in the Akure Speaking Communities, the leadership and members of Afenifere, the Ondo State Government and people, as well as the Yoruba nation. “We pray that Almighty God grants the bereaved family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss and grants the departed patriarch eternal rest. “Although Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti may have departed this earthly realm, his ideals, sacrifices, wisdom, and contributions to humanity will remain indelibly engraved in the annals of our history,” the statement said. The organisation added: “Akureland has lost a patriarch. Yorubaland has lost a distinguished leader. Nigeria has lost an elder statesman. But his legacy shall end

item.title: (Video) UNN Party Tragedy: How I regained consciousness, found friends lying lifeless – Survivor
item.description: By Emmma Nnadozie A 24-year-old student of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, has recounted how he narrowly escaped death during an off-campus party that claimed the lives of four students in Nsukka, Enugu State. The survivor, an Art Education student, said he lost consciousness after one of the participants vomited during the party, only to regain consciousness several hours later and discover his friends lying motionless on the floor. Recounting his experience with our Crime Editor, the student said the gathering was organised by his friend, David, to celebrate the completion of his final examinations. According to him, the host bought two bottles of alcoholic drinks, Magic Moment and Best, which they took to his residence at Hilltop, Nsukka, where about 10 people gathered for the celebration. He said the party started around 11:30 a.m., adding that the participants shared the drinks while engaging in a Truth and Dare game for entertainment. He narrated: “During the party, one of the participants started vomiting. I took him to the toilet and asked him to clean himself up. I then came out to clean the vomit on the floor. “After that, I suddenly lost consciousness. However, I noticed that my legs had become stiff, and I could no longer walk. “When I regained consciousness at about 9 p.m., I heard someone saying that a ghost was shaking. I woke up and managed to look into the parlour, where I saw the host and other participants lying on the floor.” The survivor said he immediately contacted a friend, who came to the house, saw their condition and left. He expressed disappointment that another person who reportedly arrived at the scene started recording them instead of making efforts to rescue them. He said he subsequently contacted another friend, who came and helped convey them to Bishop Shanahan Hospital and other hospitals in Nsukka for medical attention. Explaining the circumstances surrounding the gathering, the survivor said the participants were inside the parlour with the doors and windows shut, while a generator was operating outside in the corridor. The student dismissed suggestions that the participants might have taken illicit drugs, insisting that alcohol was the only substance consumed at the gathering. “We didn’t smoke, and there was no drug there. We took only alcohol. We had just two bottles for about 10 people, so the quantity each person drank was very little, not even up to a quarter of a party cup,” he said. The survivor, who disclosed that his legs were still stiff despite gradual improvement in his condition, said the university’s Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Simon Otuanya, had visited him to ascertain his state of health. item.title: Regulators, private sector leaders, others to review local content growth
item.description: Regulatory authorities, private sector leaders and legislators have concluded arrangement for a closed-door Local Content Roundtable to review Nigeria’s journey path of localizing its industries over the years. The engagement, driven by the Practical Nigerian Content (PNC) Forum 2026, is designed to shift the national conversation from indigenous participation to sustainable, in-country capacity development. It would also focus around the team: ‘‘Building Sustainable Local Capacity: Scaling Capability, Enabling Ownership and Funding Growth’’, and will confront the issue of physical, technological or intellectual capacity created in Nigeria since the inception of the policy in 2010. “Every year at PNC, we celebrate the percentage. This year, we wanted a room that explores what that percentage is made of, and how we build on it,” said Wemimo Oyelana, Portfolio and Country Director, dmg events, organizers of the meeting. He stated further: “The skills, technology and industrial capacity developed through projects over the past 16 years are real assets. The Roundtable will bring stakeholders together to define what lasting Nigerian capacity looks like, how it can be measured, and how we grow it at scale.” According to the organizers, PNC 2026 will bring together policymakers, industry leaders, investors and indigenous businesses to address the priorities shaping the next phase of Nigerian Content development. For operators and project developers, the discussions will examine how local capacity can support project delivery and long-term competitiveness. item.title: My mother wanted me married, not playing football – Flamingos captain
item.description: Flamingos captain, Harmony Chidi, has revealed how her mother initially opposed her ambition to become a professional footballer and wanted her to get married following the early death of her father. The 17-year-old, who led Nigeria to a historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, said her grandmother and foster father played crucial roles in keeping her football dream alive despite the opposition. Nigeria defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to become the first African country to win the competition. Speaking in an interview with BBC Pidgin, Chidi said her mother was initially unwilling to allow her to pursue football after the death of her father, but her grandmother stood by her and encouraged her to continue. “When I started football, my mother didn’t want me to play. My father died early, so my mother wanted me to get married. It was my grandmother who stood by me and pushed me to play football. Unfortunately, my grandmother is late,” she said. The Bayelsa Queens striker also credited her foster father, Prince Chidi, owner of her grassroots team, Imo Strikers, for providing the encouragement and support she needed to pursue her ambition. “It wasn’t easy until I met my foster father, Prince Chidi. He is the owner of my grassroots team, Imo Strikers, and he encourages me, making sure that I achieve my dream,” she added. Chidi also recounted how a career-threatening injury nearly ended her football ambition and prevented her from featuring at the previous edition of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. She described the injury as the most difficult period of her career, saying the experience was made worse by the withdrawal of friends who had previously been around her. “There is nothing that has been more difficult than my injury. It is an injury that has killed the dream of many players in Nigeria. All my friends deserted me and it was tough. I even thought of an alternative plan,” she recounted. However, the teenager overcame the setback, returned to action and eventually captained Nigeria to its historic world title in Morocco. Despite the milestone achievement, Chidi said she was determined to reach greater heights, naming Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Raphinha and Nigerian women’s football star Asisat Oshoala as players she admired and hoped to surpass. “I have like five players that I want to be like: Victor Osimhen, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Raphinha and Asisat Oshoala. I want to be greater than them,” she said. The post My mother wanted me married, not playing football – Flamingos captain appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Elumelu backs Nigeria’s N52,500 pension floor, praises
item.description: industry-funded retiree healthcare Chairman of Heirs Holdings and Transcorp, Mr. Tony Elumelu, has said that the PenCare Retiree Healthcare Initiative and the National Minimum Pension Guarantee will address two fundamental concerns of every retiree: access to healthcare and security of income. Elumelu who stated this while giving his remarks at the Presidential Pension Security Initiatives Launch in Abuja noted that the private sector stands ready to support policies and partnerships that strengthen our institutions. It will be recalled that Nigeria has started paying a guaranteed minimum pension of N52,500 a month to retirees in the Contributory Pension Scheme, the system of individual retirement accounts for workers. The provision has been in the country’s pension law since 2004 but was never used. President Bola Tinubu also launched PenCare, a free healthcare plan for low-income retirees that the pension industry pays for. Elumelu called the two programmes “investments in human dignity.” The Minimum Pension Guarantee takes effect immediately and will be run by the National Pension Commission (PenCom). He particularly praised the pension industry for funding PenCare, calling it “a powerful demonstration of what responsible institutions can achieve when they put people first.” PenCom Director-General, Omolola Oloworaran said 173,209 retirees currently receive less than N52,500 and will be raised to that level. Some had been receiving just over N20,000 a month. The guarantee is paid from a N400 billion Pension Protection Fund, to which the federal government and the pension industry have contributed. State governments must also pay in before their retirees can benefit. “If people are not contributing, we’ll run out of funds,” Oloworaran said. She said the N52,500 figure “was not plucked from the air. It has been validated by an actuary and it is subject to review and it is funded.” The post Elumelu backs Nigeria’s N52,500 pension floor, praises appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Amupitan denies owning pro-APC X account
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has denied owning or operating an X account allegedly used to express support for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) during the 2023 general election. Amupitan said the controversy had been referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the office of the Inspector-General of Police, adding that an independent investigative report had also been obtained. He spoke on Thursday during a dialogue at Chatham House in London, organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative, with the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” Responding to a question on whether an independent investigation had established that he was not behind the disputed account, the INEC chairman said the matter had been reported to the relevant security agencies. “We have an independent report and the matter was also reported to the DSS as well as to the IG,” he said. Amupitan maintained that he had never operated an X account, explaining that his attempt to contact the social media platform to address the allegation was unsuccessful because he was not a registered user. “I never had an X account. I tried to get in touch with X, but there’s no way if you don’t have an account,” he said. He further disclosed that some civil society organisations had expressed interest in investigating the controversy. Insisting that he had never operated the disputed account, Amupitan said his regular email platform was Yahoo. “I have my Yahoo mail. I check Yahoo mail. It was never my account. And that is the truth,” he said. The INEC chairman also suggested that the timing of the controversy was part of an attempt to discredit him and undermine the electoral commission, linking its emergence to a court ruling concerning the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the interpretation of the status quo ante bellum order. “Remember the background. That issue came up when the court ruled that ADC had an issue, and the concept of status quo ante bellum. I don’t want to go back into it. But at the same time, it came about that time,” he said. He added that attempts to discredit the commission could be channelled through attacks on its leadership. “The only way that people could bring down an institution was to say, ‘Oh, this person,’” he said. Amupitan also dismissed other allegations previously levelled against him, including claims that he was a member of President Tinubu’s legal team and that he made false claims about his educational background. He said investigations by the DSS and the police had established that the allegations were unfounded. “There were several accusations before then. item.title: Doherty warns against underestimating Obi’s influence after attack on NDC supporters
item.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, has warned politicians against underestimating Peter Obi’s political influence, saying the former Anambra State governor still commands a strong support base despite his defection from the Labour Party. Doherty said the resistance by NDC supporters to an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday showed that the enthusiasm which defined Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign remained strong. He spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today following the disruption of the meeting at Classic Event Place, Oregun, Ikeja. Dismissing suggestions that Obi’s defection to the NDC could weaken his political appeal, Doherty argued that his popularity was rooted in his political philosophy rather than the party under which he contests elections. “The reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. This is a man who is loved by the people. They view him as a different kind of politician, for good reason, and those of us who align with that philosophy and thinking,” he said. He cautioned those seeking to downplay Obi’s political relevance, describing such a position as a grave mistake. “Anybody who is making a contrary case, time will tell. But I would advise them that if they are saying that just to downplay his significance, I think it will be a grave mistake on their part because his support base is still strong. I have seen it, not just today, we have seen it multiple times,” he added. Doherty said the reaction of supporters to the attack was evidence that Obi’s political movement had not lost the energy it demonstrated during the 2023 election. He said the attackers might have expected supporters to abandon the venue in fear, but were instead confronted by people determined to defend their rights. “Those guys came in today probably thinking they would have an easy ride of it. They would come in and do what they might normally do, scatter things and people would run away. But people were not in that frame of mind,” he said. He described the attack as “unprovoked” and “unnecessary” and praised supporters who resisted the assailants, calling them heroes. Suspected political thugs reportedly invaded the venue ahead of Obi’s arrival, allegedly armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones. They vandalised property and damaged several vehicles parked within the premises. The confrontation disrupted activities before security operatives intervened. The meeting later proceeded, with Obi, Senator Victor Umeh, activist Aisha Yesufu and other party figures in attendance. item.title: INEC to obey court on Atiku’s ADC candidacy – Amupitan
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said it will abide by the final court decision on former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s eligibility to contest the 2027 presidential election on the platform of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, said the commission was constitutionally obligated to comply with court orders, particularly decisions of the Supreme Court, irrespective of their political implications. Amupitan spoke on Thursday during a dialogue at Chatham House in London, organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative, with the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” Responding to a question on whether Atiku could contest on the ADC platform if the judgment nullifying the leadership of the faction led by former Senate President, David Mark, was upheld, Amupitan said INEC would be guided by the outcome of the legal process. “If he eventually fails, well, I’m obligated under Section 285 of the Constitution of Nigeria to obey every court order, especially if it is from the Supreme Court,” he said. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had advocated an accelerated hearing of the ADC leadership dispute when it emerged in April, insisting that the matter should be resolved within three weeks to avoid complications for the 2027 electoral process. “When it happened in April, the position of the commission was that the matter should be resolved within three weeks,” he said. He explained that INEC had complied with a court directive to suspend action and await the determination of the dispute, which subsequently proceeded on appeal. Amupitan also expressed concern over the growing number of election-related cases involving the commission, disclosing that INEC had more than 300 pending court cases with the 2027 elections about 66 days away. “Some of those issues we have with court cases, over 300 cases hanging on the neck of INEC, and elections is just about 66 days away,” he said. He disclosed that INEC had commenced procurement of sensitive materials for the 2027 elections, stressing the need for reforms to ensure that pre-election disputes were resolved between six months and one year before polling. According to him, early resolution of such disputes would allow the commission sufficient time to complete its logistical and operational preparations for elections. The INEC chairman further acknowledged that the commission often faced public criticism when implementing judicial decisions but maintained that it was bound by the law. The development comes amid the protracted leadership crisis in the ADC, which has thrown the party’s preparations for the 2027 general elections into uncertainty. item.title: Violent campaigns
item.description: Barely two months to the 2027 general elections, there are rising cases of political violence across Nigeria, despite efforts by various bodies to discourage mayhem before, during and after the polls. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled to hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Assembly elections have been slated for February 6, 2026. In the last seven days, there have been cases of political violence in no less than seven states, with the latest in Lagos, where several supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) were injured after suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised on Thursday by the party for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. There was also an incident in Zamfara State during an All Progressives Congress (APC) primary. INEC will obey court verdict on Atiku’s eligibility – Amupitan How 4 UNN students died after graduation party Other states that recorded violence within the period included Edo, Delta, Gombe and Cross River states. The incidents have been more frequent this year, with states like Katsina, Kebbi, Enugu, Ekiti, Ondo, Ebonyi, Osun and Nasarawa states all experiencing various forms of political violence. Prominent political actors have also threatened voters in ways that raised concerns over free, fair and credible polls in 2027. The National Peace Committee revealed recently that reports spanning August 19 to October 27 documented 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. It also observed that political violence and thuggery led the violations with 33 incidents, closely followed by 29 cases of misinformation and disinformation and identified Kaduna, Edo, and Enugu as serious flashpoints for electoral violence. The European Union (EU) also expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of Nigeria’s general elections. EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, noted that these threats undermined democratic progress and discouraged citizens from participating freely in the electoral process. Daily Trust gathered that NDC supporters had arrived at the venue as early as 8am to prepare the hall ahead of the arrival of party leaders, including Obi and Kwankwaso, when the incident occurred. item.title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
item.description: Key US lawmakers on Thursday called for clarity on what the Trump administration knew about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chip giant announced his departure. Huang, now Nvidia’s former CEO, had pushed for looser rules on sales of US chips to China — crucial in the AI race — and the controversy has reenergized advocates of a hard line on Beijing, days before Donald Trump travels to China. “Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put US national security at risk,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on social media. “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset,” he added. Huang, a co-founder of the AI chip giant, on Sunday acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence suspects her of working for Beijing, which has strongly denied the allegations. ‘Obvious Threat’ According to The New York Times, Trump was informed of the suspicions last year, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said on Monday he knew “the FBI is looking into” the affair, adding that he expected Huang to be “in good shape.” He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy. U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP Huang was ultimately brought down by the scandal on Thursday, when the company’s board announced his departure, effective immediately. Lawmakers are also raising questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to impose restrictions on exports of the chips to China. Three Republican House committee chairmen had already said they wanted to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January after winning the midterm elections, have also said they intend to look more closely into the affair. The top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees told Lutnick in a letter on Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s “scheme to approve and tax” Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms linked to Beijing’s government and military. They accuse Lutnick and Trump of ignoring the “obvious national security threat” posed by the ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence agent, even though they had reportedly been informed of them. item.title: My Ambition Is To Ensure Tinubu’s 2027 Victory, Says Matawalle
item.description: The Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, says his major ambition is to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. Matawalle made this known while addressing supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at his residence in Gusau, Zamfara State, ahead of the expected visit of the First Lady, Senator Remi Tinubu. He urged party members to unite and intensify mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election, as well as the victory of other APC candidates in the state. The minister commended Tinubu’s efforts in tackling insecurity, developing infrastructure and promoting political cohesion, expressing his commitment to ensuring that the President completes his eight-year tenure. Matawalle said that after discharging his responsibilities as Minister of State for Defence, particularly in the fight against insecurity, his next major priority would be to work towards Tinubu’s re-election. He also dismissed what he described as provocations and propaganda by individuals seeking to tarnish his image, insisting that his priority was to sustain unity within the APC in Zamfara and secure victories for the party at all levels. The minister further dismissed allegations and propaganda concerning Tinubu’s health, maintaining that the President was fit to continue providing leadership and direction for the country. On security, Matawalle assured Zamfara residents that the Federal Government would deploy additional security personnel along major highways to protect commuters from persistent bandit attacks. He specifically mentioned the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway, as well as the Gummi-Anka-Bukkuyum and Tsafe access roads, as routes that would receive increased security attention. “We will deploy security forces along the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway to ensure the safe movement of commuters. We will also deploy security personnel to ensure the safety of those travelling along the Gummi, Anka, Bukkuyum and Tsafe roads,” he said. Matawalle pledged to do everything within his capacity to address insecurity in Zamfara and other parts of the country. He also spoke on the controversy surrounding the rerun election in Zamfara North Senatorial District, dismissing allegations of attempts to undermine his political standing and create divisions within the APC. The minister questioned the rationale behind the violence reportedly recorded during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji, insisting that political disagreements should not lead to attacks or destruction. “Those who caused the crisis during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji know whether they can emerge victorious or not. If victory is on your side, what is the essence of creating a crisis? We will not fight or attack anybody,” he said.
